newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy funds see good October after September blip.
newsitem.headline: Italy funds see good October after September blip.

text.p: Italian mutual funds are likely to see total net inflows rising again in October after a slight fall in September, which broke the postive trend seen all this year.
According to a Reuter survey of fund managers, several said Ocotober was set to be the best month so far. Official data for October inflows are due to be published on November 7.
Bond and money market funds continued to dominate investor interest with equity funds seen as less attractive.
But San Paolo Fondi said, "although inflows are mainly into Italian bond funds there appears to be return to a positive balance in national equity products."
San Paolo saw mid-October net inflows already over 1.8 trillion lire, well above inflows for the whole month of September of 1.43 billion. It said inflows since January had topped 11 trillion lire.

Fondigest also saw a clear improvement for non-bond and money market funds. Fund manager Marco Avoledo said "investors are returning to share funds but it will take a long time for a full recovery in this sector."

Giovanni Cevenini, managing director of Genercomit, said he expected October net inflows at "more than double" the 202 billion lire in September, due partly to the contribution of three new no-load products.

Arca saw an "excellent" month, with net inflows of over 300 billion lire after a poor 161 billion lire in September. Arca managers said there was little interest in equities and foreign products although "a strong lira and falling rates could perhaps prompt investors to take the opportunity to diversify."
Fideuram also expected October to be one of the year's best months, with inflows seen above 300 billion lire.

Romagest saw inflows of over 130 billion lire from 93.5 billion in September and saw the improving trend continuing in November, while for December "we could see a halt when Italians realise the weight of the government's tough 1997 budget."
